chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Armani, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever listens attentively to a speaker has worshipped him. So if the speaker is conveying from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he has worshipped Allah; and if the speaker is conveying from Satan, he has worshipped Satan.

key_terms.أَصْغَى: Listened attentively or inclined the ear
key_terms.نَاطِقٍ: Speaker or one who conveys a message

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of listening to a speaker in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni uses this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq to elevate auditory attention from a passive act to an active theological stance, framing 'istima'' (listening) as a form of devotion. This principle is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence regarding music and singing, where the content and source of the sound determine whether the listener aligns with divine truth or satanic distraction.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Ibrahim Al Arzamy, form Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who listens to a speaker to, he has worshipped him. So if the speaker is inviting from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic so he has worshipped Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, but if the speaker was inviting from the Satan<sup>la</sup> so he has worshipped the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 24. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Ibrahim al-Armaniy from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one listens to a speaker he worships him. If the speaker conveys from Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, he has worshipped Allah; but if he conveys from Satan he has worshipped Satan.’”
